summary: The unrestricted finite-template clause in the second sentence of Theorem 4.14 is false. An all-full K2 disjoint-union K1 template is a counterexample. The reduced classification, blow-up consequence and inspected dependency of Theorem 1.3 survive.

problems.title: The unrestricted-template wording in Theorem 4.14 requires a reduced representative

source_claim.claim: Every non-uniform template G has a complete or empty underlying finite graph.

assumptions: Non-uniformity of its infinite blow-up under induced-isomorphism consistency
No reduced hypothesis in the second sentence

counterexample.hypothesis_verification: The blow-up is two disjoint countably infinite cliques; a fair block order with uniform independent internal orders is consistent and non-uniform.
counterexample.claimed_result: The one-edge three-vertex graph would have to be complete or empty.
counterexample.correct_result: It is neither; Pr(a1<c1<a2)=0 under the consistent block law instead of 1/6.
counterexample.analytic_general_check: For any induced subgraph with r,s>0 vertices in the two components, each allowed block order has mass 1/(2 r! s!); isomorphisms and restrictions preserve the law.

counterevidence: The prior paragraph says reduction suffices, giving a valid intended-representative reading.
The counterexample is not reduced and does not challenge the first sentence.
The weaker blow-up consequence is true and is the only classification consequence used by Theorem1.3.
The acquired 2015 arXiv v1 omits the false intermediate finite-template assertion.
problems.impact: Local scope assertion only; no demonstrated damage to Theorem1.3 or the infinite-blow-up classification.

correction.statement: For any non-uniform template T, T_infinity is a disjoint union of cliques or a complete multipartite graph.
correction.support: Reduce T preserving its blow-up, then apply the reduced classification and label restrictions.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The full-labelled one-edge graph K2 disjoint-union K1 is allowed by the PDF p9 definition. Its blow-up is two infinite cliques. Independently assign a fair block order and independent iid-uniform rank orders within the components. For every finite induced graph with r,s>0 the allowed labelled orders have mass1/(2r!s!), invariant under induced isomorphisms and restriction; a clique alone has its uniform order. Thus this is a genuinely consistent nonuniform law, whereas the finite template is neither complete nor empty. The printed second sentence on p19 re-quantifies any nonuniform template, so the counterexample applies. The adjacent full twins merge into two full nonadjacent vertices, preserving the blow-up. Source p20 only needs the correct hereditary blow-up classification in Theorem1.3. Major core-damage is not established; Minor rests on that dependency analysis, not repair difficulty.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The preceding reduced-representative convention and the valid first sentence explain the intended statement. The report explicitly distinguishes the acquired publisher PDF from arXiv v1; no assertion against all versions.
independent_verification.repair_check: Replace the finite-template assertion with the blow-up classification, or apply complete-or-empty only to its reduced representative. This follows by the explicit twin merger and the original reduced classification.
